title: Harira Soup
historical_context: Harira is a traditional North African soup deeply rooted in Moroccan culinary heritage. Historically prepared during Ramadan to break the daily fast at sunset (Iftar), this nutrient-dense dish combines tender meat, pulses, and warming aromatic spices to quickly restore energy.
summary: Our take on a classic Moroccan soup is so substantial that it's a borderline stew! Either way, it's the ideal warming meal.
ingredients: 300g (10oz) lamb neck, cut into bite-sized chunks
2 sticks of celery, leaves and all, chopped
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan. Pat the meat dry with kitchen towel, and season with salt. Once the oil is hot, add the meat to the pan and reduce the heat slightly. Stir to brown on all the sides. Remove and then set aside.
Reduce the heat, add the onion to the pan and fry it until soft, adding a splash more oil if necessary. Stir in the garlic and spices, and cook until fragrant.

Return the meat to the pan with the chickpeas, lentils, celery and preserved lemon. Pour over the tinned tomatoes and the water. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer with the lid on for 1 hr, remembering to stir occasionally.

If using noodles, add 350ml (12fl oz / 1½ cups) of water to the pan, bring to the boil and cook the noodles for 10 mins. You may wish to add extra water to make the broth more liquid. This will be necessary if reheating.
Serve in bowls and top with the yoghurt and coriander. Add a squeeze of lemon juice, if you like.

title: Chicken & Avocado Caesar Salad
historical_context: The original Caesar Salad was invented in 1924 by Italian-American restaurateur Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico, during a busy Fourth of July weekend. Modern high-protein adaptations incorporate sliced chicken breast and nutrient-rich avocado, merging classic emulsified Caesar dressing with contemporary health-conscious ingredients.
summary: Get your protein hit from a classic Caesar salad with a twist - this one includes some vitamin-packed avocados.
ingredients: 1 head of romaine lettuce or 2 cos heads (roughly chopped)
steps: For the dressing, put all the ingredients except the oil and Parmesan into a food processor and whizz until smooth. With the motor running, gradually add the oil until you have a smooth dressing. Stir in the Parmesan and set aside (this will keep in the fridge for three days).
Toss together the lettuce, chicken and avocado, and stir through the dressing. Top with the crispy fried onions and serve.

title: Herring Smørrebrød
historical_context: Smørrebrød dates back to the 19th century in Scandinavia, originating as a simple worker's lunch of dark rugbrød (rye bread) topped with preserved fish or cold cuts. Over generations, it evolved into an iconic Danish culinary art form, featuring meticulously artistic layers of pickled herring, beetroot, horseradish, and fresh dill.
summary: A classic Danish, open-faced sandwich, perfect for lunch or a light summer supper.
steps: To make the pickle, heat the vinegar with the salt, sugar, mustard seeds, star anise and bay leaf. Once the sugar has dissolved, remove from the heat and stir in the sliced cucumber. Set aside to marinate and cool.
To make the dip, blend beetroot, walnuts, horseradish sauce, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, garlic, crème fraîche, and sumac in a food processor and season well.
To assemble the smørrebrød, spread 2 tbsp beetroot dip on each slice of rye bread, then top with herring, pickle, fresh dill sprigs and extra crème fraîche, if you like.

title: Mackerel Superfood Salad
historical_context: Mackerel has been a staple of coastal Atlantic and British cuisine for centuries due to its abundance in cold ocean waters. Modern British nutrition-focused cuisine pairs grilled oily fish with fiber-heavy pulses, mustard, and fresh vegetables to create an omega-3-rich meal.
summary: Mackerel is an oily fish hero that is packed with beneficial omega-3s.
ingredients: 400g (14oz) can mixed bean salad (drained and rinsed)
Small handful of chopped mint (some reserved for garnish)
2 courgettes (finely sliced lengthways with a peeler)
1 red chilli (finely diced, some reserved for garnish)
steps: Heat the grill to medium. In a bowl, mix together the mustard, 2 tsp oil, the lemon zest and juice.
Put the mackerel on a wire rack and cover with two-thirds of the mustard paste. Grill for 2 mins on each side, cool a little, then flake.
Meanwhile, cook the broccoli for 3 mins, then drain.
Gently mix the beans with the mint, courgettes, most of the chilli, remaining oil, remaining mustard paste and vinegar.
Arrange the beans, courgette and mackerel on plates and garnish with mint and chilli.

title: White Bean & Tomato Salad
historical_context: Legume-based salads and stews have formed the foundation of Egyptian daily sustenance since antiquity. Inspired by traditional Middle Eastern and North African mezze dishes like Ful Mudammas and Salatat Fasolia, this recipe utilizes simple pantry legumes seasoned with citrus, tomato purée, and aromatic za'atar.
summary: This Egyptian dish is a delicious way to enjoy protein-packed beans.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Gently cook the onions for 10 mins then add the garlic and stir through for a few mins. Add 150ml (5fl oz / ⅔ cup) water and the tomato purée. Stir well then put into a bowl, covered, to cool completely.
Stir the remaining olive oil and the lemon juice into the onions, together with the beans. Add the tomatoes and parsley. Check the seasoning and adjust to taste, then sprinkle over the za'atar.

title: Borlotti Bean & Kale Soup
historical_context: Rooted in the Italian tradition of Cucina Povera (peasant cuisine), heart-warming soups like Ribollita and Zuppa di Borlotti relied on humble, homegrown produce—specifically hearty brassicas like Tuscan kale (cavolo nero) and preserved legumes—to provide complete nutrition during cold winter months.
summary: This is light yet filling, making it perfect for any time of year. The beans are a great source of protein.
ingredients: 1 large potato (approx 350g / 12oz, cut into small chunks)
1ltr (2pt / 4 cups) hot vegetable or chicken stock
400g (14oz) tin of borlotti beans (drained and rinsed)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan. Add the onion and carrot and cook over a medium heat for about 5 mins.
Add the potato, tomato purée, thyme and bay leaves, stir well for 2 mins and then pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for about 10 mins, partially covered.
Stir in the borlotti beans and add seasoning to taste. Bring back to the boil, then put the kale on top and let it steam for 5 mins. Spoon the soup into warmed bowls and serve.

title: Veggie Boost Grain Salad
historical_context: Grain salads represent a modern culinary synthesis drawing from ancient agricultural traditions across South America (quinoa) and the Middle East (wheatberries, edamame). Popularized in contemporary health food movements, these salads highlight complex plant-based amino acid profiles and high-fiber roughage.
summary: A diet rich in fibrous 'roughage' as well as protein is good for your gut, so introducing beans, pulses and a variety of vegetables is beneficial.
ingredients: 250g (9oz) cooked, mixed grains (e.g., Merchant Gourmet Quinoa, lentils and wheatberries)
steps: Blanch edamame beans in boiling water for 2 mins, refresh under cold running water. Put grains in a large bowl. Mix the dressing ingredients and stir through the grains.
Add the remaining ingredients and serve.

title: Poke Bowl
historical_context: Poke (meaning 'to slice' or 'cut crosswise' in Hawaiian) originated as a traditional native Hawaiian preparation of raw, seasoned reef fish. In the 1970s and subsequent decades, Asian immigration introduced soy sauce and sesame, ultimately morphing into the globalized multi-ingredient plant and protein grain bowls popular today.
summary: This colourful lunch bowl is filled with delicious protein.
steps: Cut the tofu up into 2.5cm (1in) squares.

Add the soy sauce, lime juice, sesame oil and ginger paste into a medium bowl and then whisk together. Add the cubed tofu to the bowl and coat with the sauce. Put to one side to marinate for at least an hour.
Cook the rice and edamame beans (if frozen) according to the instructions on the packet.
Grate the carrots. Fill bowls with rice then add the remaining ingredients in sections over it. Drizzle any remaining marinade. Garnish with sesame seeds and coriander.

title: Tofu Skewers & Noodle Salad
historical_context: Satay-style skewers and fresh vermicelli noodle salads are staple street food elements across Thailand and Vietnam. Tofu, introduced to Southeast Asia via early Chinese trade routes, became a vital plant-based protein staple embraced in regional vegetarian practices.
summary: A tasty combo of beautifully marinated tofu with a crunchy, Asian-inspired salad.
steps: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 20 mins. Cut the tofu into cubes and mix together with 3 tbsp chilli sauce, the lemongrass paste, lime juice and zest, then thread onto skewers and set aside.

In a large bowl, mix the noodles, carrots, cucumber, spring onions and basil. In a separate bowl, mix the remaining chilli sauce, the soy sauce, sesame oil and 2 tbsp water, drizzle over the noodles and stir.
Cook the skewers on a medium high heat for 2 mins on each side in a frying pan or griddle pan. Serve with noodles and top with cashews.

title: Smashed Avo Toast with Soft-Boiled Eggs
historical_context: Avocado toast was popularized in Australia during the early 1990s by chef Bill Granger in Sydney before spreading worldwide as an iconic brunch item. Combining avocado with soft-boiled eggs provides a complete essential amino acid and healthy fat profile.
summary: Eggs are protein-rich and one of the few foods that contain vitamin D. This dish will banish mid-morning munchies, too.
steps: Boil the eggs in a pan of hot water for 7 mins to give a lightly-set centre. Meanwhile, stone the avocados and peel and quarter them.
Put the avocado flesh in a bowl and season generously. Add the lime juice and mash well with a fork.
Toast the soda bread slices and then peel the eggs.
Spread the mashed avocado on the toast, halve the eggs and sit them on top.

title: Roasted Chickpeas
historical_context: Roasted chickpeas (known as Leblebi in Turkey and the Middle East) have been consumed since ancient Ottoman times. Originating as a durable, portable food source for travelers and soldiers, they are now widely enjoyed globally as a high-protein, fiber-rich alternative to processed snacks.
summary: A tasty alternative snack to nuts that's packed full of protein.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) / 350°F / Gas 4. Pat the drained chickpeas dry with a paper towel.
Tip the chickpeas into a bowl and drizzle over the oil, mixing well to ensure an even coverage.
Sprinkle over the spices and mix thoroughly for good distribution.
Tip the chickpeas onto an oven tray lined with baking paper, spreading them out well.
Roast in the oven for 35 mins, but give the tray a shake every 10 mins to loosen the chickpeas and ensure that they dry out evenly.
Leave to cool and serve immediately, or store in an airtight container.
